newsitem.title: USA: Counsels seek limited investigation of Senate race.
newsitem.headline: Counsels seek limited investigation of Senate race.

text.p: Two outside counsels recommended Tuesday they be allowed to conduct a limited investigation of charges of vote buying, multiple voting and fraudulent voting in last year's Senate race in Louisiana.
Following the Nov. 5 election, Democrat Mary Landrieu was declared the winner by 5,788 votes. But Republican Louis "Woody" Jenkins challenged her victory, claiming she won by fraud.
The counsels, Washington attorneys Robert Bauer and William Canfield, III, were hired by the Senate Rules Committee to determine if a full investigation of the charges by Jenkins was justified.
They recommended dismissing four of Jenkins' charges, but said three other charges were serious enough to warrant a limited investigation.

"Counsel find that certain specific claims of fraud justify a limited investigation focused on the sufficiency of the evidence -- that is, on the question of whether there is substantial competent evidence of fraud to indicate a probability that the election was wrongly certified, and that a full investigation is required," they said in a report to the committee.
The committee now must decide if it will accept their recommendations or take other action.
"The claims subject to this investigation are: vote buying; multiple voting and registration and voting by ineligible persons," Bauer and Canfield said.
